Minimum Array End.statement: Find the smallest final element of n strictly increasing positive integers whose bitwise AND equals x.
Minimum Array End.brute: Try larger integers in order, keeping those whose set bits contain x.
Minimum Array End.optimized: Place the bits of n−1 into the zero-bit positions of x, from least significant upward. The resulting number is the nth valid value.

Divisors of a Number.statement: List all positive divisors of n.
Divisors of a Number.brute: Test every integer up to n for divisibility.
Divisors of a Number.optimized: For each divisor d up to √n, emit d and n/d, counting a square root once.

Largest Element in an Array.statement: Return the greatest element of a nonempty array.
Largest Element in an Array.brute: Sort and take the final element.
Largest Element in an Array.optimized: Carry a running maximum. Replace it whenever the next element is larger.

Second Largest Element.brute: Sort distinct values and take the runner-up.
Second Largest Element.optimized: Track the largest and second largest. A new maximum shifts the old maximum into second place. Skip equal values.

Check if Array is Sorted.statement: Decide whether values are in nondecreasing order.
Check if Array is Sorted.brute: Sort a copy and compare it with the original.
Check if Array is Sorted.optimized: Compare neighbors from left to right. The pair 3,2 already proves the order fails.

Rearrange Array Elements by Sign.statement: Alternate positive and negative elements, starting positive, while preserving order within each sign. Assume equal counts.
Rearrange Array Elements by Sign.brute: Repeatedly find and remove the next required sign from the remaining input.
Rearrange Array Elements by Sign.optimized: Write positives to even output positions and negatives to odd positions, advancing each index by two.

Leaders in an Array.statement: Return values at least as large as everything to their right.
Leaders in an Array.brute: Check each candidate against its whole suffix.
Leaders in an Array.optimized: Scan right to left carrying the greatest suffix value. Collect matching leaders and reverse their order.

Count Subarrays with XOR K.statement: Count contiguous subarrays whose XOR equals k.
Count Subarrays with XOR K.brute: Extend every start position and update the XOR for each end.
Count Subarrays with XOR K.optimized: Track prefix XOR frequencies, initially one zero. At prefix p, add the count of p XOR k before recording p.

Largest Subarray with Sum 0.statement: Find the longest nonempty zero-sum interval and return its length.
Largest Subarray with Sum 0.brute: Accumulate sums for every start and end pair.
Largest Subarray with Sum 0.optimized: Store the earliest index of each prefix sum, including zero before the array. Equal prefix sums enclose a zero-sum interval.

Merge Without Extra Space.statement: Merge two sorted arrays while retaining their original capacities.
Merge Without Extra Space.optimized: Treat both arrays as one sequence. Compare and swap entries a shrinking gap apart, ending with gap one.

Count Inversions.optimized: Merge sorted halves. When the right value is smaller, every remaining left value contributes an inversion.

Reverse Pairs.brute: Test the inequality for every pair using wide arithmetic.
Reverse Pairs.optimized: For each sorted left half, advance a pointer through the sorted right half to count qualifying cross-pairs before merging.

Pascal's Triangle II.statement: Return the zero-indexed kth row of Pascal's triangle.
Pascal's Triangle II.brute: Build every preceding row by summing adjacent entries.
Pascal's Triangle II.optimized: Start with 1. From coefficient c at position i compute the next as c×(k−i)/(i+1) with adequate precision.

KMP Algorithm.statement: Find the first occurrence of a pattern in text.
KMP Algorithm.brute: Restart matching at each possible start.
KMP Algorithm.optimized: Build the pattern's prefix table. On mismatch keep the longest matched suffix that is also a prefix, then continue scanning.

Rabin-Karp / Rolling Hash.statement: Locate a pattern in a text using equal-length windows.
Rabin-Karp / Rolling Hash.brute: Compare the pattern at every possible start.
Rabin-Karp / Rolling Hash.optimized: Roll the window hash by removing the departing character and adding the new one. Verify characters on a hash match.

Design Linked List.statement: Support indexed reads, insertions and deletions in a list.
Design Linked List.example: Input: append 2, prepend 1, delete index 1 Output: get(0) = 1
Design Linked List.brute: Keep a packed array and shift elements on front insertion or deletion.
Design Linked List.optimized: Use a sentinel head and a size counter. Walk to the predecessor and rewire one link. Maintain a tail for constant-time append.
Design Linked List.optimizedCost: O(1) end insertion, O(n) indexed access

Remove Linked List Elements.statement: Remove every node holding the target value.
Remove Linked List Elements.brute: Copy the values that survive into a new list.
Remove Linked List Elements.optimized: Start at a sentinel. When the next node matches, bypass it without advancing the predecessor.

Add Two Numbers II.statement: Add two lists of decimal digits stored most significant first.
Add Two Numbers II.brute: Convert both lists to arbitrary-precision integers, add, and convert back.
Add Two Numbers II.optimized: Push digits onto two stacks. Pop from the units end, carry to the next column, and prepend each result digit.

Flatten a Linked List.statement: Flatten sorted chains joined by bottom pointers into one sorted chain.
Flatten a Linked List.brute: Collect all values and sort them.
Flatten a Linked List.optimized: Keep one head per chain in a min-heap. Relink the smallest node and insert its bottom successor.
Flatten a Linked List.optimizedCost: O(N log k) for k chains

Infix to Postfix.statement: Move each operator after its operands while preserving precedence.
Infix to Postfix.brute: Build an expression tree and emit a postorder traversal.
Infix to Postfix.optimized: Send operands directly to output. Hold operators on a stack, popping by precedence and associativity, with parentheses delimiting groups.

Prefix / Postfix Conversion.statement: Convert a prefix expression with binary operators into postfix.
Prefix / Postfix Conversion.brute: Build an expression tree and traverse it postorder.
Prefix / Postfix Conversion.optimized: Scan right to left. Push operands. At an operator pop left then right and form left, right, operator. Use token sequences to avoid repeated string copies.

Previous Greater Element.statement: For each position return the nearest strictly greater value to its left, or −1.
Previous Greater Element.optimized: Keep a decreasing stack. Pop values at most the current one. The surviving top is its answer.

Next Smaller Element.statement: Find the nearest strictly smaller value to the right, or −1.
Next Smaller Element.brute: Scan right until a smaller value appears.
Next Smaller Element.optimized: Scan from right to left. Pop values at least as large as the current value, read the top, then push the current value.

Previous Smaller Element.statement: Find the nearest strictly smaller value to the left, or −1.
Previous Smaller Element.optimized: Scan forward with an increasing stack. Pop larger or equal entries before reading the nearest smaller value.

Sum of Subarray Minimums.statement: Sum the minimum values of all nonempty contiguous subarrays, modulo 1,000,000,007.
Sum of Subarray Minimums.brute: Extend every subarray and track its minimum.
Sum of Subarray Minimums.optimized: Find each value's previous strictly smaller and next smaller-or-equal boundaries. Multiply its value by its number of possible left and right endpoints.

Baseball Game.statement: Apply score operations: + sums the last two, D doubles the last, C cancels it.
Baseball Game.brute: Replay earlier operations whenever a previous score is needed.
Baseball Game.optimized: Maintain a stack of valid scores. The example leaves 5, 10 and 15, whose sum is 30.

Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch.statement: Count students left when nobody accepts the next sandwich.
Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch.brute: Simulate rotating the queue until a full rotation fails.
Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch.optimized: Count preferences of each type. Consume sandwiches in order while the corresponding count is positive.

Shortest Subarray With Sum at Least K.statement: Find the shortest nonempty subarray reaching k, allowing negative values.
Shortest Subarray With Sum at Least K.brute: Enumerate starts and ends with a running sum.
Shortest Subarray With Sum at Least K.optimized: Keep prefix indices in increasing prefix-sum order. Remove valid fronts to shorten the interval and discard dominated backs.

Intersection of Two Sorted Arrays.statement: Return the common values of two sorted arrays, including repeated matches.
Intersection of Two Sorted Arrays.brute: Search the second array for each unused match.
Intersection of Two Sorted Arrays.optimized: Advance the pointer with the smaller value. On equality emit the value and advance both pointers.

Binary Subarrays With Sum.statement: Count binary subarrays summing to the target.
Binary Subarrays With Sum.brute: Extend a running sum from every start.
Binary Subarrays With Sum.optimized: Count earlier prefix sums equal to currentSum−goal. Seed zero with frequency one.

Count Number of Nice Subarrays.statement: Count subarrays containing exactly k odd numbers.
Count Number of Nice Subarrays.brute: Count odds as each candidate interval expands.
Count Number of Nice Subarrays.optimized: Treat each odd number as one and each even as zero. Count pairs of prefix totals separated by k.

Longest Happy String.statement: Build a longest string from given letter counts with no run of three equal letters.
Longest Happy String.brute: Enumerate legal strings and keep the longest.
Longest Happy String.optimized: Take the most frequent legal letter from a max-heap. If it would form a triple, use the next choice and restore the blocked one.

Process Tasks Using Servers.statement: Assign arrivals to the free server of lowest weight, breaking ties by index.
Process Tasks Using Servers.brute: Scan all servers to find the next eligible one for each task.
Process Tasks Using Servers.optimized: Use a free heap by weight/index and a busy heap by finish time. Release all servers finishing by the assignment time.

The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Ch.statement: Find the chair assigned to a target arrival when everyone takes the smallest free index.
The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Ch.brute: Scan chairs from zero at each arrival.
The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Ch.optimized: Sort arrivals, freeing departures at or before each arrival. Keep released chairs in a min-heap and allocate the lowest available.

Last Stone Weight.statement: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones, returning the final weight or zero.
Last Stone Weight.optimized: Use a max-heap. Pop the two largest stones and push their difference when it is positive.

Take Gifts From the Richest Pile.statement: Repeat k times: replace the largest pile with the integer square root of its size. Return the total.
Take Gifts From the Richest Pile.brute: Scan every pile for the maximum in each round.
Take Gifts From the Richest Pile.optimized: Heapify once. Pop 25 and push 5, then pop 16 and push 4. Sum the remaining weights.

Seat Reservation Manager.statement: Reserve the lowest available numbered seat and support releasing seats.
Seat Reservation Manager.example: Input: reserve, reserve, release 1, reserve Output: 1, 2, 1
Seat Reservation Manager.brute: Scan occupied seats from the start at each reservation.
Seat Reservation Manager.optimized: Track the next previously unused seat and a min-heap of released seats. Reuse the smallest released seat first.

Maximum Product After K Increments.statement: Spend k unit increments on nonnegative numbers to maximize their product, then reduce modulo 1,000,000,007.
Maximum Product After K Increments.brute: Try every distribution of the increments.
Maximum Product After K Increments.optimized: Use a min-heap to increment the smallest value each time. Equalizing small factors gives the greatest product.

House Robber III.statement: Maximize the sum of selected tree nodes while excluding parent-child pairs.
House Robber III.optimized: Return two totals per subtree: taking the root forces both children to be skipped, while skipping permits each child's better total.

Partition Array for Maximum Sum.statement: Partition into blocks of at most k and replace each block with its maximum value. Maximize the sum.
Partition Array for Maximum Sum.optimized: For each prefix try the last 1..k elements as one block. Track its maximum and combine its contribution with the earlier optimum.

Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minim.statement: Split 2n values into two size-n groups with minimum absolute sum difference.
Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minim.optimized: Split the input in halves. Group subset sums by selected count, then binary-search a complementary sum of the required size near half the total.

Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Tra.statement: Maximize profit across trades while paying the fee once per sale.
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Tra.brute: Try buy, sell and wait on every day subject to ownership.
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Tra.optimized: Carry the best cash and holding states. Update each using the preceding day's states, subtracting the fee on sale.

Count Square Submatrices with All Ones.statement: Count all square submatrices containing only ones.
Count Square Submatrices with All Ones.brute: Check every possible square cell by cell.
Count Square Submatrices with All Ones.optimized: For each one, its largest square ending there is one plus the minimum of top, left and diagonal sizes. Sum these sizes.

Matrix Chain Multiplication.statement: Choose parentheses that minimize scalar multiplications for compatible matrices.
Matrix Chain Multiplication.optimized: For each interval test the last split k. Add the two optimal subcosts and the cost of multiplying their results.

Parsing a Boolean Expression.statement: Evaluate nested boolean operators !, & and or with comma-separated operands.
Parsing a Boolean Expression.brute: Repeatedly find and replace the innermost completed expression.
Parsing a Boolean Expression.optimized: Parse once with an index or stack. At a closing parenthesis combine all values belonging to that operator.

Delete Operation for Two Strings.statement: Find the fewest deletions required to make two strings equal.
Delete Operation for Two Strings.brute: Try all pairs of retained subsequences.
Delete Operation for Two Strings.optimized: Compute the longest common subsequence length L. Delete all other characters, for a total m+n−2L.

Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence.statement: Count index-distinct subsequences with maximum strictly increasing length.
Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence.brute: Enumerate all increasing subsequences, keeping counts at the greatest length.
Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence.optimized: At each endpoint store its best length and count. A better predecessor replaces the count, and an equally long predecessor adds to it.

Longest String Chain.statement: Find the longest chain where each new word inserts exactly one character.
Longest String Chain.brute: Try all word sequences and check predecessor relations.
Longest String Chain.optimized: Sort by length. Delete each character in turn and look up the best chain ending at the resulting shorter word.

Largest Divisible Subset.statement: Return a largest subset of distinct positive integers where every pair is divisible in one direction.
Largest Divisible Subset.brute: Test every subset for pairwise divisibility.
Largest Divisible Subset.optimized: Sort ascending and run longest-chain DP using divisibility as the predecessor rule. Trace parent indices to recover the subset.

DFS.statement: Visit a binary tree in depth-first preorder, processing root, left subtree, then right subtree.
DFS.brute: Use recursive calls to visit each subtree.
DFS.optimized: A stack makes the same order explicit. Push right before left so the left child is popped first.

Morris Tree Traversal.statement: Traverse a binary tree inorder using constant auxiliary space and restore its original links.
Morris Tree Traversal.brute: Use recursion or an explicit ancestor stack.
Morris Tree Traversal.optimized: Thread each left subtree's rightmost node back to its parent. On the second encounter remove the temporary thread and visit the parent.

Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree.statement: Return the smallest one-based level with the highest sum.
Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree.brute: Visit the tree once per level to compute that level's sum.
Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree.optimized: Process complete queue layers. Compare the layer sum before advancing and retain the earliest best level.

All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree.statement: Return values exactly k edges from a target node.
All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree.brute: For each node determine the length of its path to the target.
All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree.optimized: Index parent links, then run BFS from the target over parent and children. Return the frontier after k expansions.

Burning Tree.statement: Fire spreads one edge per time step. Find when the whole tree has burned.
Burning Tree.brute: Repeatedly scan all edges to find newly burning neighbors.
Burning Tree.optimized: Index each parent and start BFS at the ignition node. The last occupied layer gives the burn time.

Children Sum Property.statement: Check whether each internal node equals the sum of its immediate children, treating missing children as zero.
Children Sum Property.brute: Create a list of internal nodes, then check each local equation.
Children Sum Property.optimized: During one traversal compare each internal node with its child sum and stop at the first failure.

Binary Tree Paths.brute: Build a new path copy for every recursive call.
Binary Tree Paths.optimized: Push each visited node onto one path buffer. Copy only at leaves and pop on return.

Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree.statement: Count nodes at least as large as every ancestor on their root path.
Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree.brute: Walk the ancestor path for each node to find its maximum.
Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree.optimized: Pass the maximum seen so far down the tree and count nodes meeting it.

Largest BST in Binary Tree.statement: Return the node count of the largest subtree that is a strict binary search tree.
Largest BST in Binary Tree.brute: Validate and count the subtree rooted at every node.
Largest BST in Binary Tree.optimized: In postorder return validity, minimum, maximum and size. Join children only if their ranges fit strictly around the root.

Floor in BST.statement: Return the greatest BST key no larger than the target.
Floor in BST.brute: Scan all keys and track the best eligible key.
Floor in BST.optimized: At a key ≤ target save it and go right. At a larger key go left.

Ceil in BST.statement: Return the smallest BST key at least the target.
Ceil in BST.brute: Scan every key and compare eligible candidates.
Ceil in BST.optimized: Save a key ≥ target and go left to improve it. Otherwise go right.

Inorder Predecessor in BST.statement: Find the largest BST key strictly less than a given key.
Inorder Predecessor in BST.brute: Materialize an inorder traversal and locate the previous key.
Inorder Predecessor in BST.optimized: Descend from the root, saving smaller keys before moving right. For a greater or equal key, go left.

Two Sum IV — Input is a BST.statement: Determine whether two distinct tree nodes sum to k.
Two Sum IV — Input is a BST.brute: Test every pair of distinct nodes.
Two Sum IV — Input is a BST.optimized: Walk the tree with a seen set. Before inserting v, check for k−v, so one node cannot pair with itself.

Recover Binary Search Tree.statement: Restore the BST after the values of two nodes were swapped.
Recover Binary Search Tree.brute: Sort all values and rewrite the inorder sequence.
Recover Binary Search Tree.optimized: Scan inorder for decreasing adjacent pairs. Swap the first offending predecessor with the last offending current node.

Search in a Binary Search Tree.statement: Return the node with a requested key if it exists.
Search in a Binary Search Tree.brute: Visit nodes without using their ordering.
Search in a Binary Search Tree.optimized: Compare at the root and retain only the left or right subtree indicated by the key.

Insert into a Binary Search Tree.statement: Insert a new distinct key while preserving BST order.
Insert into a Binary Search Tree.example: Input: tree=[8,4,12], key=6 Output: 6 becomes the right child of 4
Insert into a Binary Search Tree.brute: Collect and sort keys, then rebuild the tree.
Insert into a Binary Search Tree.optimized: Follow comparisons to a missing child and attach the new leaf there.

Delete Node in a BST.statement: Delete a key while preserving search order.
Delete Node in a BST.brute: Copy all remaining keys and rebuild.
Delete Node in a BST.optimized: Find the key. Splice out a node with at most one child. With two children, replace its key with its inorder successor and delete that successor.

Construct Binary Search Tree from Preord.statement: Reconstruct a BST with distinct keys from its preorder sequence.
Construct Binary Search Tree from Preord.brute: Insert the keys one by one into a new BST.
Construct Binary Search Tree from Preord.optimized: Read preorder once with a shared cursor. Each subtree consumes the next keys that fit its permitted range.

Trie — Insert, Update, Search, Delete.statement: Maintain a word dictionary through character-by-character paths.
Trie — Insert, Update, Search, Delete.example: Input: insert car, insert cart, delete car Output: contains car=false, cart=true
Trie — Insert, Update, Search, Delete.brute: Store words in a list and compare whole strings for each lookup.
Trie — Insert, Update, Search, Delete.optimized: Follow one edge per character and mark terminal nodes. Update terminal data in place. Delete by unmarking and pruning only unused suffixes.
Trie — Insert, Update, Search, Delete.optimizedCost: O(L) per operation with constant-time child lookup

BFS of Graph.statement: Visit vertices reachable from a source in increasing edge distance.
BFS of Graph.example: Input: A→B, A→C, B→D; start A Output: A, B, C, D
BFS of Graph.brute: Repeatedly scan all vertices and edges for the next distance layer.
BFS of Graph.optimized: Use a queue and mark vertices when enqueuing them. Expand every outgoing edge once.

Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph.statement: Find the fewest edges from a source to every reachable vertex.
Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph.example: Input: A—B—C, A—C; start A Output: A:0, B:1, C:1
Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph.brute: Enumerate simple paths and keep the shortest to each vertex.
Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph.optimized: Run BFS and assign each vertex its distance on first discovery.

DFS of Graph.statement: Explore reachable vertices by following each path as far as possible before backtracking.
DFS of Graph.example: Input: A→B, A→C, B→D; visit B first Output: A, B, D, C
DFS of Graph.brute: Recursively scan a full adjacency matrix for neighbors.
DFS of Graph.optimized: Store adjacency lists and a visited set. Recurse or use explicit stack frames to finish each neighbor before moving to the next.

Find if Path Exists in Graph.statement: Decide whether two vertices in an undirected graph are connected.
Find if Path Exists in Graph.example: Input: edges=[[0,1],[1,2]], start=0, end=2 Output: true
Find if Path Exists in Graph.brute: Enumerate simple paths until a connection appears.
Find if Path Exists in Graph.optimized: Start DFS or BFS at the source and mark each vertex on discovery. Stop when the destination is found.

Keys and Rooms.statement: Starting in room zero, use collected keys to determine whether every room can be opened.
Keys and Rooms.brute: Repeat full scans of unlocked rooms looking for new keys.
Keys and Rooms.optimized: Treat keys as directed edges. Visit each newly unlocked room once and compare the visited count to the total.

As Far from Land as Possible.statement: In a binary land/water grid, find the water cell farthest from its nearest land by Manhattan distance.
As Far from Land as Possible.brute: Compare each water cell against every land cell.
As Far from Land as Possible.optimized: Start BFS from all land cells at once. The final water layer has the greatest nearest-land distance. Handle all-land and all-water grids separately.

Number of Enclaves.statement: Count land cells unable to reach the grid boundary by four-directional moves.
Number of Enclaves.brute: Test boundary reachability separately from each land cell.
Number of Enclaves.optimized: Flood all boundary land inward, then count land untouched by that flood.

Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using D.statement: Detect a cycle in a simple undirected graph using depth-first traversal.
Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using D.example: Input: A—B, B—C, C—A Output: cycle
Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using D.brute: Remove each edge and test whether its endpoints remain connected.
Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using D.optimized: In each component use DFS with a parent. A visited neighbor other than the parent closes a cycle.

Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using B.statement: Detect a cycle in a simple undirected graph while exploring by layers.
Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using B.example: Input: A—B, B—C, C—A Output: cycle
Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using B.brute: Remove each edge and test whether another path joins its ends.
Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph using B.optimized: Queue vertex-parent pairs and mark on discovery. A seen neighbor other than the parent proves a cycle.

Topological Sort using DFS.statement: Order vertices of a directed acyclic graph so each dependency comes before its dependent.
Topological Sort using DFS.example: Input: A→C, B→C Output: B, A, C (one order)
Topological Sort using DFS.brute: Try permutations and validate the direction of every edge.
Topological Sort using DFS.optimized: Track unseen, active and finished vertices. An active back-edge signals a cycle. Otherwise reverse the finish order.

Kahn's Algorithm / BFS.statement: Produce a dependency order by removing vertices with no unsatisfied prerequisites.
Kahn's Algorithm / BFS.example: Input: A→B, A→C Output: A, B, C (one order)
Kahn's Algorithm / BFS.brute: Repeatedly scan remaining edges to find an eligible vertex.
Kahn's Algorithm / BFS.optimized: Queue all zero-indegree vertices. Remove one, decrement its neighbors' indegrees, and enqueue any that reach zero. A short output signals a cycle.

Find All Possible Recipes from Given Sup.statement: Determine which recipes can be made when each completed recipe becomes an ingredient.
Find All Possible Recipes from Given Sup.example: Input: supplies=[flour], bread needs flour, toast needs bread Output: [bread,toast]
Find All Possible Recipes from Given Sup.brute: Repeatedly retry every unmet recipe against available ingredients.
Find All Possible Recipes from Given Sup.optimized: Count each recipe's unavailable requirements. Propagate newly available supplies through ingredient-to-recipe edges and release recipes reaching zero.

Possible Bipartition.statement: Split people into two groups so every dislike edge joins opposite groups.
Possible Bipartition.optimized: Two-color each connected component. Assign every neighbor the opposite color and reject a same-color edge.

Bipartite Check using BFS.statement: Determine whether a graph is two-colorable using a queue.
Bipartite Check using BFS.brute: Try every assignment of two colors.
Bipartite Check using BFS.optimized: Queue a starting vertex per component. Color newly seen neighbors oppositely and reject a color conflict.

Bipartite Check using DFS.statement: Determine whether a graph is two-colorable using depth-first traversal.
Bipartite Check using DFS.brute: Try all partitions and test the edges.
Bipartite Check using DFS.optimized: DFS with an expected color. Recurse into each unseen neighbor with the opposite color and verify already colored neighbors.

Number of Provinces using DSU.statement: Count connected groups in an adjacency matrix.
Number of Provinces using DSU.brute: Compute transitive closure, then group reachable cities.
Number of Provinces using DSU.optimized: Start with one set per city. Union connected pairs from the matrix, decrementing the group count on successful merges.

Number of Operations to Make Network Con.statement: Find the fewest redundant cables to move so all n computers are connected, or return −1.
Number of Operations to Make Network Con.brute: Try cable moves and recompute connectivity after each trial.
Number of Operations to Make Network Con.optimized: If there are fewer than n−1 cables, connecting all nodes is impossible. Otherwise count components and return components−1.

Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Col.statement: Remove a stone if another remaining stone shares its row or column. Maximize removals.
Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Col.optimized: Union row and column identifiers separately for each stone. Every connected component can retain exactly one stone.

Making a Large Island.statement: Flip at most one zero in a binary grid to maximize a four-connected island.
Making a Large Island.brute: Flip each zero in turn and flood-fill the entire grid.
Making a Large Island.optimized: Label islands and record their sizes once. For each zero add one and the sizes of distinct neighboring island labels.

Number of Islands II.statement: Report island counts after each land insertion, ignoring duplicate insertions.
Number of Islands II.brute: Recount connected components after every insertion.
Number of Islands II.optimized: Give each new cell its own DSU set and increment the count. Each successful union with a land neighbor reduces it by one.

Swim in Rising Water.statement: Find the earliest time at which start and finish connect through cells with elevation at most the time.
Swim in Rising Water.brute: Test every distinct water level with a fresh flood-fill.
Swim in Rising Water.optimized: Use a priority queue for a minimax path: extending a path costs the larger of its current level and the new cell's elevation.

Kruskal's Algorithm.statement: Connect a weighted undirected graph with minimum total spanning-tree weight.
Kruskal's Algorithm.example: Input: AB=1, BC=2, AC=4 Output: 3 via AB and BC
Kruskal's Algorithm.brute: Enumerate spanning trees and compare totals.
Kruskal's Algorithm.optimized: Sort edges by weight. Use disjoint sets to accept only edges that join different components until V−1 edges are chosen.

Prim's Algorithm.statement: Grow a minimum spanning tree in a connected undirected weighted graph.
Prim's Algorithm.brute: Try spanning trees and compare their total weights.
Prim's Algorithm.optimized: Grow from one vertex. Repeatedly accept the lightest crossing edge from a heap, skipping stale edges whose endpoints are already in the tree.
Prim's Algorithm.optimizedCost: O(E log E) with an edge heap

Word Ladder II.statement: Return all shortest single-letter transformation sequences through dictionary words.
Word Ladder II.example: Input: hit→cog; hot,dot,dog,lot,log,cog Output: hit-hot-dot-dog-cog and hit-hot-lot-log-cog
Word Ladder II.brute: Enumerate all simple transformation paths, then retain the shortest.
Word Ladder II.optimized: BFS by levels and record every predecessor on a shortest path. Backtrack that predecessor graph from the target.
Word Ladder II.optimizedCost: BFS graph work plus output enumeration

Dijkstra's Algorithm.statement: Compute single-source distances in a graph with nonnegative edge weights.
Dijkstra's Algorithm.example: Input: A→B:5, A→C:1, C→B:2 Output: A=0, C=1, B=3
Dijkstra's Algorithm.brute: Scan all unsettled vertices to select the one with the smallest distance.
Dijkstra's Algorithm.optimized: Use a min-heap keyed by tentative distance. Skip stale entries and relax outgoing edges from each best-known state.
Dijkstra's Algorithm.optimizedCost: O((V+E) log V) for a simple graph

Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination.statement: Count minimum-time routes in a positive-weight road network, modulo 1,000,000,007.
Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination.brute: Enumerate simple paths while keeping the best cost and tie count.
Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination.optimized: Run Dijkstra with a count per vertex. A shorter route replaces the count, an equally short route adds to it.

Bellman-Ford Algorithm.statement: Compute distances from one source even with negative edges, and detect reachable negative cycles.
Bellman-Ford Algorithm.example: Input: A→B:4, A→C:5, B→C:−2 Output: A=0, B=4, C=2
Bellman-Ford Algorithm.brute: Enumerate all simple paths for each destination when there is no reachable negative cycle.
Bellman-Ford Algorithm.optimized: Relax every edge up to V−1 rounds. A further reachable improvement proves a negative cycle.

Negative Weight Cycle Detection.statement: Detect whether any directed cycle in a weighted graph has negative total weight.
Negative Weight Cycle Detection.brute: Enumerate simple cycles and sum their weights.
Negative Weight Cycle Detection.optimized: Initialize every distance to zero, equivalent to a super-source. A relaxation on the Vth round of Bellman-Ford proves a negative cycle.

Floyd-Warshall Algorithm.statement: Find all-pairs shortest distances when there is no negative cycle.
Floyd-Warshall Algorithm.example: Input: A→B:2, B→C:3, A→C:8 Output: distance A→C = 5
Floyd-Warshall Algorithm.brute: Run Bellman-Ford independently from every source.
Floyd-Warshall Algorithm.optimized: For each intermediate k update d[i,j] with min(d[i,j], d[i,k]+d[k,j]). Put the k loop outermost.

Find the City With Smallest Number of Ne.statement: Find the city reaching the fewest other cities within a distance threshold. Break ties by larger city index.
Find the City With Smallest Number of Ne.brute: Enumerate paths to test reachability for every city pair.
Find the City With Smallest Number of Ne.optimized: Compute shortest distances, count entries within the threshold excluding the city itself, then apply the tie rule.

Strongly Connected Components.statement: Partition a directed graph into maximal groups whose vertices reach one another.
Strongly Connected Components.brute: Test mutual reachability for every vertex using repeated traversals.
Strongly Connected Components.optimized: Kosaraju uses DFS finish order then traversal on reversed edges. Tarjan uses discovery indices, low links and an active stack to emit each component in one DFS.

Bridges in Graph.statement: Find undirected edges whose deletion disconnects their component.
Bridges in Graph.example: Input: triangle ABC with edge C—D Output: C—D
Bridges in Graph.brute: Remove each edge and recount components.
Bridges in Graph.optimized: During DFS store discovery and low-link times. A tree edge to child v is a bridge if low[v] exceeds discovery[parent]. Track the parent edge by identity.

Articulation Points.statement: Find vertices whose deletion increases the number of connected components.
Articulation Points.brute: Delete each vertex and recount components.
Articulation Points.optimized: A non-root DFS vertex is a cut point if a child cannot reach any earlier ancestor. A DFS root needs at least two tree children.

Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm.statement: Maximize feasible source-to-sink flow in a network with integer capacities.
Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm.brute: Enumerate feasible integer edge flows and test conservation.
Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm.optimized: Find a residual s-to-t path, push its bottleneck, and add reverse capacity so earlier choices can be revised. Stop when no path remains.
Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm.optimizedCost: O(EF) for integral maximum flow F

Edmonds-Karp Algorithm.statement: Compute maximum flow by augmenting along shortest residual paths in edge count.
Edmonds-Karp Algorithm.brute: Try all source-side cuts and select the smallest capacity.
Edmonds-Karp Algorithm.optimized: Use BFS to find each residual augmenting path. Push its bottleneck and update forward and reverse edges until the sink is unreachable.

Minimum Cut.statement: Partition source and sink to minimize total capacity of edges leaving the source's side.
Minimum Cut.example: Input: s→a:3, a→t:2, s→t:1 Output: cut {s,a} → {t}, capacity 3
Minimum Cut.brute: Try every vertex partition with source and sink on opposite sides.
Minimum Cut.optimized: Compute maximum flow. In the final residual network mark vertices reachable from the source. Original edges leaving that set form a minimum cut.

Build Heap.statement: Turn an unsorted array into a max-heap. Every parent must be at least as large as its children.
Build Heap.brute: Insert values one at a time, bubbling each up to its position.
Build Heap.optimized: Start at the last internal node and sift each parent down. Short subtrees dominate the total work.

Heap Sort.statement: Sort an array in ascending order using its own storage.
Heap Sort.brute: Repeatedly scan the unsorted prefix to find its maximum and move it to the end.
Heap Sort.optimized: Build a max-heap. Swap the maximum into the last unsorted position, shrink the heap, and sift its new root down.
Heap Sort.optimizedCost: O(n log n), O(1) extra with iterative sift-down
